enemies.summary: Ork Boyz are the many warriors that make up the backbone of the Orks armies. There are many types of Boyz, and not a lot of distinction between them. enemies.summary: Also known as Grots, or Runts they share many similarities with their bigger, stronger clan mates. They ruefully serve the stronger Orks, their size being their main hindrance in advancing the ranks. Some even operate their own black-market businesses. Synonymous with cunning, and with a lack of any real physical prowess, these very un-Orky creatures are still a menace on the battlefield, with their flashy blastas and sharp stabbas.

enemies.summary: Larger than a Boy and smaller than a Warboss, the Nobz have some authority over their peers. Arrogant, cruel Orks who love to boss around a mob of Boyz with impunity, they wield a variety of deadly weapons. But nothing looks better than a good 'ol flashy Shoota, maybe with a kustom job from an affordable Mek.

enemies.title: Warbiker
enemies.summary: Part of the Kult of Speed, these Orks are also known as Speed Freeks, and are entirely addicted to storming into battle as fast as they possibly can. Featuring Nitro-Squig fuel injektors, ultraboomerz blasting some good ol' Goff Rock, huge spoilers and billowing exhaust vents, these Warbikers are more than capable of upending the battlefield and looking way flashier than their mates whilst doing it.

enemies.title: Warbikers
enemies.summary: There are few things Orks love as much as fighting, but going fast is one of them. Warbikers are addicted to the thrill of hurtling towards their enemies with all guns blazing.

enemies.title: Bomb Squig
enemies.summary: Living weapons of Ork design, these squigs are loaded with explosives. Stuffed and strapped with anything the Orks have on hand, everything from Tankbusta bombs to pressure mines, and a good helping of Stikkbombs. Through rudimentary training they are taught to chase down enemy tanks, fearlessly and without any sense of self-preservation.

enemies.title: Killa Kan
enemies.summary: Small Orkish walkers, made by Meks and Painboyz. Crude in their appearance, but complex in their design, they are piloted by a Gretchin, eagerly wired into the large metal cans. The power and glory of their newfound strength carry them through battlefields, stomping on whatever gets in their way.

enemies.title: Loota
enemies.summary: Thievin’ Orks who will pinch any and every piece of weaponry they can get their hands on. Meks use this stolen weaponry to make their fearsome Deffguns. These guns are strapped to the Lootas broad shoulders, and fire high calibre dakka than can easily pierce even the thickest armour.

enemies.title: Big Mek with Shokk Attack Gun
enemies.summary: The best laid plans and blueprints are nothing compared to Mek who knows what’s what. Cobbling together whatever feels right in the moment, constantly tinkering and experimenting with their creations, Meks produce some of the weirdest, and the most powerful weapons the Orks use. The Shokk Attack Gun is no exception. The Shokk Attack Gun fires small Snotlings, hurled through a warp portal, appearing on top of the Orks enemies. The terrified snotlings then tear into anything they happen to emerge in front of, on top of, or even inside of their foes. A truly shocking experience for the unsuspecting.

enemies.summary: Ghazghkull Mag Uruk Thraka, Prophet of the Waaagh! is a fearsome warlord of the Goff Klan, and long-time nemesis of Commissar Yarrick. His lust to see the green tide swell means he ventures on, subjugating every clan and Warboss under his banner.

enemies.title: Makari
enemies.summary: Makari is perhaps the luckiest Grot there ever was, serving the glorious Goff Warboss Ghazghkull Thraka. Seen to follow his master into battle, wielding Da Lucky Stikk - a Bosspole adorned in bloody symbols drawn by Makari himself - Makari remains dutifully at Ghazghkull’s side. Despite many accusations to the contrary.

enemies.title: Warboss Squig
enemies.summary: Squigs (short for “squiggly beasts”), are the simplest form of Orkoid life. They only possess animalistic instinct and a ferocious appetite, which does have its uses in combat - especially when a large bomb is strapped to them.

enemies.title: Runtherd
enemies.summary: These callous taskmasters of the Oddboyz are as malicious as the next Ork, forcing Grots to the front lines relentlessly with their Grabba-Stikks and Grot Prods.

enemies.title: Plague Marine
enemies.summary: Transforming the best of transhuman traits into their most virulent forms, these soldiers embody Nurgle's putrescent gifts. These infernal blessings give them nightmarish abilities to spread disease and decay through sanctified enviro-seals. Though they specialise in short-range munitions, they do still wield their boltguns, sodden with corruption.

enemies.title: Mortarion, Daemon Primarch of Nurgle
enemies.summary: Daemon Prince of Nurgle and betrayer of the Emperor, Mortarion leads the Death Guard. To merely stand in his presence is to endure a barrage of plagues, to challenge him is to risk everything. Flying into battle on decayed wings, to personally command his gene-sons. He swings his colossal scythe, dubbed Silence, for that is all that is left in his wake.

enemies.title: Great Unclean One
enemies.summary: Greater Daemons of Nurgle, they are said to be moulded in the image of the Plague God. Malfeasant antlers crown their round heads, and their lasciviously grinning mouths drip with putrid slime. Serving as generals in Mortarion's army, they wield great corroded blades that cleave enemies. Their true strength lies in their putrid, rotund bodies. Unfortunate souls find themselves crushed beneath their immense weight, or swallowed whole to rot in their massive stomachs.

enemies.title: Nagash, Supreme Lord of the Undead
enemies.summary:
The Undying King, Supreme Lord of the Undead, and the Great Betrayer are just some of the titles Nagash has been known by. He is the incarnation of darkness, the creator of the foul art of Necromancy and ruler of the realm of Shyish. In battle, he wields artefacts of great power – Alakanash, the staff through which he channels his necromantic power. Zefet-nebtar, his cursed blade. And above all, through the Nine Books of Nagash, he commands the awesome and terrible magic of the Realm of Death.
To face him is to face death itself. And though victory may be had, death comes for us all eventually.
